findings.doc_quote: Each next run is calculated from wall-clock time, not from the previous run time.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/scheduler/triggers.py:346-348 — `def next_run_time(self, previous_run, current_time): return self.advance_past(previous_run, current_time)`; src/hassette/core/scheduler_dispatch.py:174 — `next_run = job.trigger.next_run_time(job.next_run, date_utils.now())`
findings.explanation: The next run is computed from the previous logical run time (`job.next_run`), advanced by whole intervals until it is after the current time. Wall-clock time is only used to skip missed ticks. Because the anchor is the scheduled time rather than the moment the handler ran or finished, the interval does stay drift-resistant, but the stated source of the calculation is backwards.
findings.suggested_fix: Each next run is calculated from the previous scheduled time, not from when the handler ran or finished, skipping any ticks already missed. The interval stays drift-resistant under load.

findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/scheduler/triggers.py:121-123 — `parts = at.split(":")`, `if len(parts) != 2: raise ValueError(f"{label} 'at' must be 'HH:MM', got {at!r}")`; Daily calls it at triggers.py:398. Runtime probe: `Daily(at="07:00:30")` raised `ValueError: Daily 'at' must be 'HH:MM', got '07:00:30'`
findings.explanation: `run_daily` passes `at` to `Daily`, which accepts only two colon-separated fields. An "HH:MM:SS" value raises ValueError.

findings.doc_quote: These parameters are accepted by every scheduling method.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/scheduler/scheduler.py:515-528 — `register` has no `jitter` or `where` parameter; scheduler.py:214 — `def add_job(self, job, *, if_exists="error")` accepts only `if_exists`
findings.explanation: The `run_*` methods and `schedule` accept all of these parameters. `register` lacks `jitter` and `where`, as line 109 of the same page says, and `add_job` takes only `if_exists`. Line 4 of the page counts `add_job` among the scheduling methods, so the sentence is too broad.
findings.suggested_fix: These parameters are accepted by schedule() and every run_* method. register accepts a subset (see its table), and add_job takes only if_exists.

findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/scheduler/scheduler.py:670-671 — `if not name: raise SchedulerNameRequiredError(callable_name(func), str(trigger))`; src/hassette/exceptions.py:704 — `class SchedulerNameRequiredError(HassetteError)`. Runtime probe: `issubclass(SchedulerNameRequiredError, ValueError)` returned False
findings.explanation: An empty name raises SchedulerNameRequiredError, which derives from HassetteError and not ValueError. `except ValueError` will not catch it.

findings.doc_quote: | jitter | float | None | 0 | Random offset in seconds added to each run.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/scheduler/scheduler.py:596 — `jitter: float | None = None`; the same default appears on every run_* method, e.g. scheduler.py:799
findings.explanation: The default is None, not 0. The runtime effect is the same, because `apply_jitter` returns the time unchanged for None or zero (src/hassette/scheduler/classes.py:559).
findings.suggested_fix: Change the Default column for jitter to None.

findings.doc_quote: Overrides the app-level handler set via scheduler.set_error_handler() .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/scheduler/scheduler.py:190 — `def on_error(self, handler: "SchedulerErrorHandlerType") -> None:`. Search: `grep -rln set_error_handler src docs` matched no files under src/ (the check's `---` separator followed immediately, with no paths listed)
findings.explanation: Scheduler has no `set_error_handler` method. The app-level handler is registered with `scheduler.on_error(handler)`, so calling the documented name raises AttributeError.
findings.suggested_fix: Overrides the app-level handler set via scheduler.on_error().

findings.doc_quote: Invoked on any exception, including CancelledError .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/core/command_executor.py:352-354 — `except asyncio.CancelledError: enqueue_result_record(); raise`, which exits before the handler spawn at command_executor.py:540-556 (`if (result.is_error or result.is_timed_out) and result.exc is not None:`)
findings.explanation: CancelledError is recorded and re-raised, so the error handler is never invoked for it. The handler runs for regular exceptions and for TimeoutError.
findings.suggested_fix: Invoked on any exception, including TimeoutError but excluding CancelledError.

findings.doc_quote: The monitoring UI shows this record alongside predicate_description and human_description on the job.
findings.explanation: The job detail view renders one description: human_description, falling back to predicate_description. It never shows both. I checked this view only; the claim that skipped records appear in the UI was not separately traced through the frontend.
findings.suggested_fix: The monitoring UI shows this record alongside the job's predicate description (human_description, falling back to predicate_description).

findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/cli/__init__.py:74 — `apps_app = App(name="app", help="List and inspect apps.")`; __init__.py:114 — `apps_app.command(cmd_app_reload, name="reload")`. No top-level `reload` command is registered in __init__.py:69-99. src/hassette/cli/commands/app.py:231 defines `cmd_app_reload`, and docs/pages/cli/commands.md:148 documents `hassette app reload <key>`
findings.explanation: There is no `hassette reload` command. The reload command is `hassette app reload <key>`, and it takes a required app key.

summary: The method signatures, parameter defaults, trigger validation, predicate behavior and if_exists semantics are mostly accurate. The nine errors cluster in the shared-parameters table (lines 117-125) and in stray references elsewhere: an unsupported HH:MM:SS format for run_daily, a nonexistent `hassette reload` command, and a backwards description of how run_every computes its next run. The most damaging are the wrong exception for an empty name, the nonexistent `set_error_handler()`, and the false claim that on_error runs on CancelledError.
